angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 452,205 km at 101.85 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.8184 +/- 0.0233 mas (same row, RUWE 1.41): 101.85 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.65 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract): 452,205 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.69 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4339 +/- 92 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156..277L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-126.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.651, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
